verdict.tagline: Surviving as a dinosaur demands patience through a very rough start.
for_you_if: you want deep survival mechanics with proximity voice chat
you can handle steep learning curves and harsh progress loss
not_for_you_if: you will not troubleshoot anti-cheat and launch failures
you need in-game maps and tutorials to get started
you are unwilling to manually change game version branches

citations.review_text: Super hard to understand... hard to play... even downloading it and trying to play it... there's two version apparently??? you have to go online to see a walkthrough of how to play the one that actually works.. like wtf?? and when playing... there's no one on the island, no resources... dead game in my opinion.. The Isle — Quite possibly the worst "game" I've ever played.
The Isle promises the fantasy of living as a dinosaur, but delivers shallow gameplay, unimpressive physics, lifeless NPCs and an uninspired world. Its minimalism feels less like a commitment to realism and more like a lack of imagination.

Graphics and Physics
The graphics aren't terrible, but they're hardly impressive. Worse is the apparent absence of basic collision between creatures.
I can walk through corpses. I can walk through living dinosaurs. I can walk straight through my friend.
Nothing says "living, breathing prehistoric ecosystem" quite like dinosaurs phasing through one another.

Servers and Population
There seem to be plenty of players, just not in my region. Most populated servers I found were in China; the Australian ones were practically deserted - pretty sure i know why. 
The busiest local server I encountered had about ten players. That's a problem for a game built around encounters with other players.

Gameplay — Minimalism or Minimal Effort?
Eat. Drink. Rest. Walk. Run. Attack. Make four different calls. Press a button to reveal scents, water, footprints and a compass. Repeat until your baby dinosaur grows into an adult through three growth stages.
That's the gameplay loop I experienced.

I understand the ambition: an authentic dinosaur survival simulator. But there's a difference between deliberate minimalism and simply having very little to do.

There's no map, no quests, not even introductory journeys. I can already hear it: "You're a dinosaur! Dinosaurs don't have maps or quests!"
Fair enough. 
But the game already displays instructional prompts explaining night vision and senses. How would introductory journeys teaching those same mechanics be any less authentic? Both are artificial guidance systems.
You know what else dinosaurs don't have? A compass. A character sheet displaying genetics and biological needs. Or an invisible camera floating behind them.

And that last point matte…

citations.review_text: Fun, would like in game map

The game is pretty entertaining solo, loads more fun with friends even in spite of some nuisances. Those nuisances being bugs here and there during gameplay, which is expected as it's early access, another is the lack of there being an in-game map. Websites have a map where you can find out where you are and where you're going, but if players do this why isn't there at least a placeholder map for in-game yet to eliminate the consant Alt+Tab just to head to the website in order for me to know where I am?

Those 2 issues (lack of a map and the bugs), are the only downsides I have. Graphics look beautiful, the dino's look pretty good, and it seems easy for a few hours to pass by when playing the game. *FOR NEW BUYERS* Be sure to change the default version of the game to EVRIMA-Public Branch since this is the current updated version of the game. I made that mistake myself when I first played. Game runs smooth for me on high settings, usually achieving minimum of 100FPS.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as having a steep learning curve and being very difficult when starting out.

citations.review_text: This game is really hard but fun.
you need to give it time to gain skill but once u have its the best

the isla is really fun and an awesome game there are still a lot of glitches but there working on that its also pretty hard when your first starting but it gets easier as you play it more and learn the game 

i really recommend this game its tones of fun :)

I mostly got this game because i saw a lot of VOIP videos on social media. Although the base game doesn't have that, there are some great servers out there that do (shoutout to Bosch Island).

The game has a steep learning curve, and it can be hard to survive. But there's also a lot of great guides out there and a lot of friendly players willing to teach you.

As for the gameplay, it does have to be in your taste. It can be very harsh, Dinos take long to grow and your life can end in a second without warning. Making you start all the way from the beginning again.

I personally love the game, as it's the growing process that keeps us busy, planning, and active in the game. It allows us to get into and create the situation we enjoy and laugh about. And to be very honest, it felt very good hitting my first Prime Elder dinosaur after about 60 hours of learning, dying and socializing.

8/10.
- Needs some work, but in development. Eating and interactions can be a bit buggy (as expected)
- The graphics are beautiful and feel of the island are very nice and calm, but at the same time terrifying.
- Performance is still a bit of an issue, with a crash every here and there (nothing too bad, maybe 2 crashes in like 15 hours of gametime)
- The dinosaurs sound absolutely amazing
- A lot of the controls are well done and comfortable (especially flying)
- Some spawn zones are a bit limited or almost certain doom for your dinosaur (not sure if this is a per server thing)

TIP: Switch your resolution to fullscreen/windowed fullscreen, and then back. In my case this seems to fix a bug and restores my fps from around 60 to 80 back to around 110/130

Also remember that Pachys are evil and you should slime them on sight.
it's a survival game so don't be discouraged when you die. super fun game. a bit of a learning curve at first but once you've got it, it's fun and very detailed

Creature spawns randomly turn off even when there's under 60 people in a server and none of them are accessible, you'll get your dinosaur spawned into the center of trees and rocks, there's still a multitude of areas where I've gotten stuck between a slope and solid ground where I've gotten animation locked into a perpetual sliding state, the hitboxes are a joke, and the penalty system for different actions genuinely just feel like you're getting punished for playing the game at some point. claims.claim: Reviewers highlight that the game features proximity voice chat servers which create an enjoyable and funny social experience.

citations.review_text: really fun game plenty of options for which dino you want to be and how you want to play. Good headphones and sound card are important so you can tell where exactly noises are coming from. The voice chat servers are also soo much fun as there is a great community

I mostly got this game because i saw a lot of VOIP videos on social media. Although the base game doesn't have that, there are some great servers out there that do (shoutout to Bosch Island).

The game has a steep learning curve, and it can be hard to survive. But there's also a lot of great guides out there and a lot of friendly players willing to teach you.

As for the gameplay, it does have to be in your taste. It can be very harsh, Dinos take long to grow and your life can end in a second without warning. Making you start all the way from the beginning again.

I personally love the game, as it's the growing process that keeps us busy, planning, and active in the game. It allows us to get into and create the situation we enjoy and laugh about. And to be very honest, it felt very good hitting my first Prime Elder dinosaur after about 60 hours of learning, dying and socializing.

8/10.
- Needs some work, but in development. Eating and interactions can be a bit buggy (as expected)
- The graphics are beautiful and feel of the island are very nice and calm, but at the same time terrifying.
- Performance is still a bit of an issue, with a crash every here and there (nothing too bad, maybe 2 crashes in like 15 hours of gametime)
- The dinosaurs sound absolutely amazing
- A lot of the controls are well done and comfortable (especially flying)
- Some spawn zones are a bit limited or almost certain doom for your dinosaur (not sure if this is a per server thing)

TIP: Switch your resolution to fullscreen/windowed fullscreen, and then back. In my case this seems to fix a bug and restores my fps from around 60 to 80 back to around 110/130

Also remember that Pachys are evil and you should slime them on sight.

Yes it can be buggy BUT I highly recommend getting a server that does PROX chat. It becomes a lot more fun that way and there are some hilarious moments. I have meet some really cool people here.

citations.review_text: If you've ever played VR chat and thought to yourself "There's not enough death in here" then this is the game for you... for just $20 you too can spend 3 hours growing a dinosaur just to lose it to 17 Vietnamese T-rexes for trying to stay hydrated. Highly recommend. 10/10

Not Recommended: The better you get, the less you actually play.

I have over 300 hours in The Isle, and I genuinely wanted to love this game. In many ways, I did. The concept is fantastic, the dinosaurs are impressive, and the survival mechanics can be incredibly engaging. Unfortunately, the more experienced I became, the more I realized that the game has a fundamental problem: the best way to survive is to avoid actually playing it.

Progression requires hours of real-world time spent growing your dinosaur, managing your diet, and developing mutations. But all of that investment can disappear in seconds, often in an encounter where you have little or no realistic chance of surviving.

As you become more experienced, you learn to avoid unnecessary risks. You stop exploring, stop hunting other players, and avoid fights unless you're certain you can win. Eventually, you realize that the safest strategy is to find somewhere isolated, eat just enough to survive, and spend hours waiting for your dinosaur to grow.

And the worst part? Once you've finally reached adulthood, you have even more to lose, giving you even less incentive to take risks.

You can try playing more aggressively, actively hunting and maintaining your diets to grow faster, but that exposes you to players who can erase hours of progress in an instant. You can play cautiously, but then you're spending most of your time hiding instead of enjoying the game. Neither option feels particularly rewarding.

The obvious solution is to join a large group, but that fundamentally changes the experience and shouldn't be a requirement for enjoying the game.

I understand that The Isle is intended to be a hardcore survival game. I don't object to permadeath, difficulty, or meaningful consequences. The problem isn't that dying is punishing. It's that the game increasingly rewards avoiding the very gameplay that makes it worth playing.

So why did I spend over 300 hours playing a game I'm giving a nega…
